Subject: BrightHealth - pricing schedule question and netting request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the draft order form. Legal had a quick read and flagged two items we want to discuss before we move to signature: (1) netting of overage credits across adjacent billing periods, and (2) whether the "commit anchoring" language in Exhibit C allows BrightHealth to apply credits to Dedicated capacity invoices.

Proposed ask from our side: can Redwood provide a clause that permits netting of credits generated from month-to-month overages within a rolling 60-day window, and confirm credits can be applied to Dedicated invoices when the account is in good standing? We also attached Exhibit C v2 (PDF) with marginal notes.

If you can share a redline with your suggested language, that would speed things up. We are aiming to close this week.

Samir — thanks for the note and the markup. Appreciate the objective (close this week).

Quick summary of our side so we are aligned before legal redlines:
- We are open to a 60-day rolling netting window but need to preserve a minimum monthly commitment floor that triggers true-up if not met over quarter.
- Credits can be applied to invoices tied to Dedicated capacity so long as there is no outstanding delinquent balance greater than 30 days.
- We prefer to keep netting scoped to token/usage credits (not to be fungible with professional services or third-party pass-through charges).

Irene — looping you for proposed contract language. Rishi tagging for commercial approval if we move the floor/true-up mechanics.

Next step: Irene to propose a tracked-redline for Exhibit C which we can drop into the Drive and route back to Samir for sign-off.

Thanks,

Samir / Marissa — attaching our proposed redline (RI_proposed_ExhibitC_redline_v3.docx). Below are high-level legal comments and the specific wording I recommend inserting into Exhibit C. I kept the change set minimal to avoid reopening unrelated commercial terms.

1) Netting window and scope
Proposed insertion (Exhibit C, new section 3.2):
"3.2 Netting of Usage Credits. Notwithstanding any other provision, Credits generated by usage overages shall be eligible for netting against subsequent Usage Charges incurred by Customer during the sixty (60) day period following issuance of such Credits (the \"Netting Window\"). Credits shall only be netted against Usage Charges for the Services (text generation, embeddings, and related inference requests) and shall not be applied to Professional Services, third-party pass-through fees, or taxes."

Rationale: limits scope, ties to your ask for a 60-day rolling window.

2) Application to Dedicated invoices and delinquency carveout
Proposed insertion (Exhibit C, amendment to section 4.1):
"Credits may be applied to invoices for Dedicated Capacity Services provided Customer does not have an outstanding unpaid balance that is more than thirty (30) days past due. Any remaining Credit balance after application to an invoice will remain available subject to the Netting Window."

Rationale: preserves Redwood collections protections while honoring BrightHealth's request to apply credits to Dedicated invoices.

3) Minimum floor and quarterly true-up
We recommend adding a brief cross-reference to the Order Schedule: if Customer's billed Usage Charges fall below the Minimum Monthly Commitment for two consecutive months within a calendar quarter, Customer will be subject to the quarterly true-up mechanism described in Section 5 (True-Up), which remains unchanged. This prevents gaming of the floor while allowing temporary netting.

4) Implementation mechanics and operational notes
- Credits will be issued as a line-item credit on the next invoice and will be labeled "Usage Netting Credit."
- For accounting clarity, netting entries will not change the underlying invoice metrics — they are credit adjustments applied post-invoice.

Please review the attached tracked redline. Key open point for BrightHealth Legal: whether the Netting Window should be 30/60/90 days. We proposed 60 to balance operational reconciliation with commercial flexibility.

If this language looks acceptable, Marissa can circulate the DOCX via Drive/DocuSign — I will stand by for any narrow edits.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RI_proposed_ExhibitC_redline_v3.docx (tracked changes)
